newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan workers demand protection of their rights.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan workers demand protection of their rights.

text.p: About 1,000 Taiwanese workers marked International Labour Day on Thursday with a march through Taipei's streets demanding government protection of workers' rights.

Shouting "Down with (President) Lee Teng-hui and (Premier) Lien Chan", the protesters, dressed as prisoners, marched from the Taipei train station toward the nearby Presidential Office but were stopped several hundred yards from their goal by riot police.
"Our activity today is to seek an end to judicial persecution of labourers," said march organizer Wang Chuan-ping, executive director of the Labor Rights Association.
She said Taiwan's assembly law, which forbids unapproved demonstrations, often resulted in workers being sued and jailed if they staged unapproved protests over labour disputes.
"We want to make our cause known in order to abolish the assembly law," Wang said.
She said Taiwan also needs to set up a labour court to handle disputes between employees and employers.
"We take the opportunity of the International Labor Day on May 1 to march on the streets, and to demand (the government) stop persecuting workers," she said.
The protesters demanded that President Lee and Premier Lien step down for failing to safeguard the rights and interests of the 5.8 million workers in Taiwan.
They also staged a skit near the Presidential Office in which a greedy judge demanded money from poor workers during a court hearing on labour disputes, but was later beheaded by the workers.
